headline: You can live on a 5-acre lot while you build, in a registered travel trailer once your house permit is issued, and later add up to 3 permitted small units. An uncertified $20,000 capsule is never a legal bedroom. Favor an unincorporated County lot, where the rules suit a tiny house built slowly.
key_points: You choose your rules when you choose the lot. Look up the lot's 13-digit Assessor's Parcel Number (APN). A lot inside the Town of Yucca Valley follows Town rules. A lot outside it (Landers, Flamingo Heights, Pioneertown, Joshua Tree and nearby areas) follows unincorporated San Bernardino County rules. Almost every rule below depends on that answer.

An unincorporated County lot suits a tiny house built slowly. The County sets no minimum house size; state code asks only for one 70 sq ft room, a bathroom and a kitchen sink. On County parcels of 5+ acres zoned Rural Living (RL), Agriculture (AG) or Resource Conservation (RC), owners may camp up to 4 days in any 30 before any permit (ask County Land Use Services (LUS) whether the days are consecutive or a total, and whether your zone suffix qualifies). The Town requires a house of at least 725 sq ft, with a 20-ft average width and two covered parking spaces. The Planning Commission revisited that rule in mid-2026, so ask Town Planning. The Town has no camping allowance.

You can live legally in a certified recreational vehicle (RV) or park trailer, a manufactured home labeled by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), factory-built housing approved by the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD), or a permitted site-built house. Most cheap imported capsules are none of these, so an uncertified capsule is never a legal bedroom in the Town or the County. Even a certified RV is legal only in an approved location, and a park trailer is not meant to be a year-round home.

You can live on the land while you build. Use an RV or travel trailer registered with the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), under a temporary permit you get once the house building permit is issued. The Town also accepts a manufactured home for this. A park model may not qualify in the County because it needs current DMV registration, so ask County LUS before buying one.

On a County lot, a small HUD-labeled manufactured home can be your first legal house. You then build the modern heated-floor house slowly as a detached accessory dwelling unit (ADU) of up to 1,200 sq ft. Once the County accepts a complete application, processing typically takes 4-5 weeks and fees average about $4,800. That figure leaves out the home, foundation, septic and utilities. Septic, water and Joshua tree clearances come first and can take much longer. The modern house then takes one of the 3 accessory-unit slots.

Whatever you finish first has to be permitted as the primary house. State law (Government Code 66328) does not let an ADU get its certificate of occupancy (the final sign-off to move in) before the primary house has one.

On a County lot of 5 acres or more, you can add up to 3 accessory units. Only one can be a guest house, and a junior ADU has to be inside the house. A detached ADU is 200-1,200 sq ft and up to 18 ft tall (20 ft if its roof pitch matches the house). It sits at least 4 ft from side and rear lot lines and must be code-built or HUD- or HCD-certified. A unit under 500 sq ft avoids both impact fees and school fees. Town ADU limits are unconfirmed (ask Town Planning).

On a County parcel of 2 acres or more, you can hold up to 2 short-term-rental permits. They can't be used for by-right ADUs, RVs or tents. The Town caps short-term rentals at 10% of single-family homes and keeps a waitlist.

You can place buildings anywhere outside the County RL setbacks: 25 ft front, 25 ft street side, 15 ft interior side and 15 ft rear. Buildings plus paving can cover up to 20% of the lot, about 1 acre of 5 acres. Buildings can be up to 35 ft tall. Town RL numbers look similar, with 25% coverage (ask Town Planning).

You can flatten pads under a County grading permit, which you need once cut plus fill passes 100 cubic yards. Hillside standards start at a 15% natural slope. Above a 20% slope you need a soils engineer, and disturbing 1 acre or more needs a state stormwater permit. In the Town, a slope of 15% or more triggers hillside review once grading passes 500 cubic yards per lot or disturbed ground passes 10,000 sq ft (about a quarter acre). No pads are allowed where the average slope is 40% or more. Keep every pad, trench and fence more than 50 ft from any western Joshua tree and you need no California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) permit.

On a County lot, you can store belongings in a shipping container with an accessory-structure permit (County Information Bulletin IB-0002, Jan 2026). The container must be painted to blend in and sit behind the main house. It needs 5 ft from lot lines and 10 ft from buildings, must stay out of the front setback, and can be at most 10 ft tall with nothing stacked on it. It can have no utilities and no one can live in it. On a lot with no house yet, it also needs a Temporary Use Permit and a removal bond. A storage unit in town is simpler until the house permit is issued. The Town allows one container on RL lots of 2.5 acres or more.

As owner-builders, you can build the house yourselves, including your own electrical and plumbing under the permit. If you pay helpers, you may count as their employer and need workers' compensation insurance; having no coverage can bring fines of up to $100,000. Anyone you hire for a job over $1,000 must hold a contractor's license. If you sell within a year of completion, you have to show you did not build the house to sell.

risks.risk: Living full-time in an uncertified capsule, or in any unit before the house permit is issued, can lead to a complaint and an order to vacate. It can also bring a notice recorded on the title, cost-recovery fees, and a hold on new permits until those costs are paid. Amnesty covers only units built before Jan 1, 2020, so a capsule placed now is not covered.
risks.mitigation: Live legally from the first night. Use a DMV-registered travel trailer under a temporary permit after the house permit is issued, or a permitted HUD home as the primary house. Until then, stay in town or within the County's allowance of 4 camping days in any 30.

risks.risk: Money spent on an uncertified imported capsule is lost, because the unit can never become a legal home, ADU or guest house.
risks.mitigation: Buy only a unit with a HUD label, an HCD factory-built insignia, or an RV Industry Association (RVIA) seal under the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1192 standard. See the vehicle identification number (VIN) and the DMV title before you pay a deposit.

risks.risk: A Town lot can break the plan. It brings a 725 sq ft minimum house and no camping. Inside the mapped sewer Phase 1 or Phase 2 areas, a septic ban also applies, with a sewer hookup required within 180 days once sewer arrives. Plan on a Phase 2 deadline of Dec 31, 2028 unless Hi-Desert Water District (HDWD) confirms Dec 31, 2031 in writing.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the jurisdiction and zone before you make an offer. For a Town lot, check the HDWD sewer map, and ask Town Planning to put the current minimum house size in writing.

risks.risk: Grading pads without a permit, or disturbing ground within 50 ft of a western Joshua tree, leads to stop-work orders and costly fixes.
risks.mitigation: Get a topographic survey and a cut/fill estimate first. Pull a grading permit before any machine work, and put pads in the gaps between Joshua trees.

risks.risk: The temporary trailer permit may end sooner than planned. The County checklist allows up to 5 years, but an older code clause reads as 12 months plus 12 more. A lapsed building permit also ends the trailer permit.
risks.mitigation: Get the County's written answer for your APN, and pass a building inspection at least every 5 months.

risks.risk: A paid helper who gets hurt can leave you liable as their employer, with fines of up to $100,000 if you carry no workers' compensation.
risks.mitigation: Hire licensed subcontractors who carry their own workers' compensation, or buy a policy before you pay anyone.

questions_for_couple: Since the capsule can't be a legal bedroom, which do we prefer: a used travel trailer during the build, or a small HUD home as our first legal house, with the modern house built later as an ADU of 1,200 sq ft or less?
Will we look only at unincorporated County lots, given the Town's 725 sq ft minimum house size and its lack of a camping allowance?
How many pods do we really want, who are they for (guests, rental income, a studio), and will we pay for certified or code-built units, ideally under 500 sq ft each?
Which work will we do ourselves, and will we hire licensed trades or pay helpers and carry workers' compensation?
What rules out a lot for us: Joshua trees on the only flat ground, slopes over 15%, a Town septic-ban area, or a very long driveway?
Before the house permit is issued, do we keep our belongings in a storage unit in town or pay for a permitted container plus a removal bond on the lot?
next_actions: Look up the lot's APN on the San Bernardino County parcel map viewer (lus.sbcounty.gov/?p=6170). Write down Town or County, the zone and its suffix (for example RL or RL-5), and any Fire Safety, Hillside or Floodplain overlay. (@computer)

Call County Land Use Services at (909) 387-8311 or (760) 995-8140 with the APN. Ask whether the temporary trailer limit is 5 years or 12 + 12 months, whether a HUD home can be the primary house with the modern house as a later ADU, whether a park model qualifies, and how the 3-unit cap counts a guest house. Ask them to send the answers by email. (@phone)

If the lot is in the Town, call Town of Yucca Valley Planning at (760) 369-6579 ext. 328 (Mon-Thu). Ask about the current minimum house size, RL setbacks and coverage, ADU limits, and container rules. (@phone)
Email the capsule seller for photos of a HUD label, an HCD factory-built insignia or an RVIA/NFPA 1192 seal, plus the VIN and DMV title. Pay no deposit until you have them. (@email)
Walk the lot and count Joshua trees and stems. Flag a 50-ft circle around each tree, and check the slope at each possible pad with a phone inclinometer app. (@land)
Ask a civil engineer or licensed land surveyor for 2 quotes covering a topographic survey, setback staking and a cut/fill estimate for the house and 3 small pads. (@email)

Ask the listing agent in writing for the permit history, any recorded code-enforcement notices, a list of every structure on the lot, and any existing percolation (perc) test. Do this before the offer planned for Jan-Feb 2027. (@email)
Check the Hi-Desert Water District sewer map to see whether a Town lot falls in sewer Phase 1 or Phase 2. (@computer)
Sketch a site plan inside the setbacks showing the house, the trailer spot, up to 3 pods under 500 sq ft each, storage and the driveway, and keep total coverage under 20%. (@together)
